strategies.name: Seasonal Compression Breakout
strategies.idea: Trade breakouts of recent ranges only in historically positive seasonal months, when volatility is compressed, creating setups for expansion moves.
strategies.rationale: Seasonal traders expect rallies in Oct/Nov for gold/silver/coffee but sit on the sidelines when vol is low. When volatility then expands in these months, breakouts run harder because option sellers are caught short and hedge funds pile in. The other side is volatility sellers (options traders) who were wrong about vol staying compressed in seasonally active months.

strategies.name: Trend Extremism Exhaust
strategies.idea: On hourly timeframe, short extreme rallies (RSI > 80) within confirmed uptrends, and go long extreme selloffs (RSI < 20) within downtrends, capturing mean reversion before trend followers get destroyed.
strategies.rationale: The trend bot loses on hourly because it extends too long into exhaustion. This trades the small counter-trend pulses that happen just before major moves reverse. Who loses: retail momentum chasers who buy every spike in uptrends without waiting for RSI exhaustion, getting trapped when smart money takes profits; also traders using mechanical stops at support who get shaken out on spikes before the real reversal.

strategies.name: Volatility Spike Reversal
strategies.idea: Fade extreme intraday moves when volatility spikes (emotional capitulation), exiting when emotion normalizes.
strategies.rationale: Volatility spikes on hourly charts mark panic selling or euphoric buying—unsustainable extremes. When vol explodes AND price is extended (rangepos near 0 or 1), weak hands are exhausting. The other side: momentum chasers who panic out once vol subsides. This captures intraday mean reversion in real time, not after-the-fact trend following.

strategies.name: Trend Extreme Catch
strategies.idea: Buy dips to the trend at multi-bar lows only when the trend is confirmed; sell bounces at multi-bar highs in downtrends.
strategies.rationale: Trend traders oversell at lows and overbuy at highs within established trends because they fear reversal. But extremes (new lows/highs on 50-bar basis) within a confirmed trend often accelerate, not reverse—weak shorts are forced to cover or margin calls hit longs. This trades the institutional liquidation cascade that happens when price reaches structure extremes in the direction of the trend.
